characters: A child with a mother at a market stall, with heaps of tomatoes, bananas, pawpaw, green leaves and yams.

narrationPlan.voice: Lively market voice with a smile
narrationPlan.pace: Lively, like a market call (about 70 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: A light shaker and a hand-drum with a market-call tune (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Markets are busy centres of food and trade in Ghanaian towns. The foods named are common but not in every home; teachers should use what children know.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check the colours and the foods for local accuracy.

teacherGuide.overview: A colour rhyme set in a market. Form: five couplets. Rhyming pairs: heap/steep, bunch/lunch, sweet/treat, buy/dry, round/sound. It teaches colour words and healthy foods.
beforeReading: Show real foods and ask children to name the colours.
whileReading: Hold up or point to something of each colour.
afterReading: Paint or colour a market scene.
discussion: Which foods are good for our bodies?
reflection: What colours are on your plate today?

support: Use real fruit and cloth swatches.
stretch: Add a verse for a purple or white food.

culturalNotes: Markets are busy centres of food and trade in Ghanaian towns. The foods named are common but not in every home; teachers should use what children know.
localiseThis: Use the foods sold at the nearest market.
